teaching_point: Classic scabies burrow on the palm: short, wavy, greyish thread-like line with a vesicle — the mite sits at the leading end. Pathognomonic sign; look here first.
dermnet_caption: A burrow on the palm - the mite can just be seen adjacent to the vesicle
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A burrow on the palm - the mite can just be seen adjacent to the vesicle (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies

teaching_point: Finger web spaces are the commonest site — scaling, papules and excoriation between the fingers in an itchy patient (esp. worse at night).
dermnet_caption: Interdigital scaling in the first web space of the hand
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Interdigital scaling in the first web space of the hand (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies

teaching_point: Small papules in the 4th web space — check every web space, wrists and flexures; household members often itchy too.
dermnet_caption: Papular lesions in the 4th interdigital space on the hand
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papular lesions in the 4th interdigital space on the hand (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies-images

teaching_point: Multiple palmar burrows — easiest to see with a magnifier/dermatoscope or the burrow ink test (ink rubbed on then wiped off tracks along the burrow).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scabies burrows on the palm (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: dark triangular 'delta-wing jet' (mite head/forelegs) at the end of the burrow 'contrail' — supports bedside diagnosis.
dermnet_caption: A dark scabies mite at the end of a burrow on dermoscopy
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A dark scabies mite at the end of a burrow on dermoscopy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies-images

teaching_point: Beltline/abdomen and groin papules — typical secondary hypersensitivity eruption; matches the Week 3 Case 1 history (wrists → web spaces → beltline/groin).
dermnet_caption: Groin and abdominal papules and pustules in scabies
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Groin and abdominal papules and pustules in scabies (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies-images

teaching_point: Itchy papules on the penis/scrotum are highly suggestive of scabies — treat sexual contacts and consider GUM/STI screening.
dermnet_caption: Erythematous papules on the penis in scabies
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythematous papules on the penis in scabies (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies-images

teaching_point: Nodular scabies in the axilla — persistent itchy nodules can last weeks after successful treatment (post-scabetic); not necessarily treatment failure.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scabies nodules in the axilla (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies

teaching_point: Infants: palms, soles, face and scalp can be involved — apply permethrin to the whole body incl. scalp/face (avoid eyes/mouth); seek specialist advice if <2 months.
dermnet_caption: Scabies burrows on a babies foot
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scabies burrows on a babies foot (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies

teaching_point: Impetiginised scabies: crusting/pustules from secondary Strep/Staph infection — treat the infection (CKS impetigo/cellulitis) as well as the mite.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scabies with superadded streptococcal infection (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies

teaching_point: RED FLAG — crusted (Norwegian) scabies: thick hyperkeratotic crusted plaques, often in elderly/immunosuppressed/care-home residents; itch may be mild. Refer urgently; highly contagious.
dermnet_caption: Thick crusted plaques on the thumb and palm due to crusted scabies in an elderly woman
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Thick crusted plaques on the thumb and palm due to crusted scabies in an elderly woman (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scabies

teaching_point: Advanced crusted scabies on the feet: gross hyperkeratosis and fissuring — needs specialist care (oral ivermectin + topical), isolation and outbreak control.
dermnet_caption: Hyperkeratosis and fissuring on the feet in advanced crusted scabies
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Hyperkeratosis and fissuring on the feet in advanced crusted scabies (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/crusted-scabies

teaching_point: Adult head louse (Pediculus humanus capitis) among scalp hairs — only finding a LIVE louse (ideally by detection combing) confirms active infestation.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Louse (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/head-lice

teaching_point: Magnified adult head louse — six legs with claws adapted to grip hair; 2–3 mm, grey-brown. Moves quickly away from light, so visual inspection alone misses many.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Louse (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/head-lice

teaching_point: Eggs/nits cemented to the hair shaft near the scalp — unlike dandruff they do not brush off. Empty nits alone do not prove active infestation.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Head lice eggs (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/head-lice

teaching_point: Nits with excoriated dermatitis at the nape — typical itchy sites behind the ears and at the nape (as in Week 3 Case 2).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Nits and dermatitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/head-lice

teaching_point: Nits plus bite papules/excoriation — scratching can lead to secondary impetigo and occipital lymphadenopathy.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Nits and bites (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/head-lice

teaching_point: Ixodes (sheep/deer) tick — vector of Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato. Bites are often unnoticed; prompt, correct removal with fine-tipped tweezers or a tick tool reduces transmission risk.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Ixodes tick (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lyme-disease

teaching_point: Erythema (chronicum) migrans: expanding red macular patch at a tick-bite site, days–weeks after the bite — diagnose and treat clinically (NICE NG95); no blood test needed.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythema chronicum migrans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lyme-disease

teaching_point: EM with central clearing ('bull's-eye') — but many EM lesions are uniformly red; enlarging over days and usually not hot, itchy or painful.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythema chronicum migrans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lyme-disease

teaching_point: Large expanding EM — contrast with a tick-bite hypersensitivity reaction, which appears and fades within ~48 h and is more often itchy/hot.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythema chronicum migrans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/erythema-migrans-images

teaching_point: EM variant appearance — annular/oval erythema in a person with possible tick exposure (gardens, parks, woodland, Scottish Highlands, southern England).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythema chronicum migrans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/erythema-migrans-images

teaching_point: Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans (late Lyme, mainly B. afzelii), inflammatory stage: bluish-red doughy discolouration of an extensor limb surface — refer/test (serology), 28-day antibiotics per NG95.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Inflammatory stage (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acrodermatitis-chronica-atrophicans

teaching_point: ACA inflammatory stage on the dorsum of the hand — violaceous, doughy discolouration often mistaken for chilblains, venous/vascular disease or ageing skin in older adults; ask about tick exposure months–years earlier.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Inflammatory stage (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acrodermatitis-chronica-atrophicans

teaching_point: ACA atrophic stage: thin, wrinkled 'cigarette-paper' skin with visible veins — late manifestation; may coexist with peripheral neuropathy.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Atrophic stage (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acrodermatitis-chronica-atrophicans

teaching_point: Cantharidin blisters: cantharidin is the vesicant in blister beetle (Meloidae) haemolymph — it causes intraepidermal blisters on an erythematous base by contact, the same mechanism as blister beetle dermatitis (shown here after therapeutic use).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cantharidin (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cantharidin

teaching_point: Therapeutic cantharidin being applied to a wart with an applicator — shows that the beetle-derived vesicant works by contact alone (no bite/sting), causing a blister within hours.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cantharidin (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cantharidin

teaching_point: Differential/look-alike — Paederus (rove beetle) dermatitis: linear erythema then vesicles/pustules with 'kissing' lesions in a flexure. Toxin is paederin (not cantharidin); the Week 3 quiz image was this pattern.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption derived from page heading
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Kissing paederus dermatitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/paederus-dermatitis

teaching_point: Paederus rove beetle (Staphylinidae): slender, orange-and-black — crushing it on the skin releases paederin. Compare with the meloid blister beetles in W05/W06.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Paedarus littoralis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/paederus-dermatitis

teaching_point: Blister beetle (Meloidae) — Lytta vesicatoria ('Spanish fly'), a classic cantharidin source. Contact/crushing on skin causes vesicles on a red base with burning within ~24 h.
licence_note: Public domain — no restrictions; credit as courtesy
attribution: Image: Lytta vesicatoria — Stefanie Hamm, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lytta-vesicatoria03.jpg

teaching_point: Mylabris blister beetle (Meloidae) — common in Mediterranean/tropical regions; ask returning travellers about beetles landing on exposed skin at night (attracted to lights).
licence_note: CC BY-SA 3.0 — share-alike; credit author and licence
attribution: Image: Mylabris oleae (Meloidae) — Hectonichus, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Meloidae_-_Mylabris_oleae.JPG

teaching_point: Papular urticaria: grouped, very itchy firm papules — a delayed hypersensitivity to bites (often cat/dog fleas or mites); bites themselves rarely noticed.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption derived from page heading
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papular urticaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/papular-urticaria

teaching_point: Papular urticaria with tense vesicles/bullae on bitten areas of the arm — intense hypersensitivity in sensitised individuals; may impetiginise if scratched.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption derived from page heading
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papular urticaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/papular-urticaria

teaching_point: Grouped red papules on the trunk/axillary area — papular urticaria can affect covered sites too (e.g. bed bugs/bird mites); crops recur and old lesions may flare with new bites.
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption derived from page heading
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papular urticaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/papular-urticaria

teaching_point: Papular urticaria on a child's lower legs — commoner in children, who usually outgrow it as they desensitise. Treat itch (topical steroid ± antihistamine) and the source (pets/home).
caption_note: DermNet alt text blank; caption derived from page heading
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papular urticaria (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/papular-urticaria

teaching_point: Flea bites: clustered itchy papules, often on lower legs or at the waistband. Treat pets with veterinary flea products and the home (vacuum, wash bedding).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Flea bites (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/flea-bite

teaching_point: Flea bites around the ankle — fleas jump to lower-leg height; clustered itchy papules, some with a central punctum or tiny blister.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Flea bites (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/flea-bite

teaching_point: Bed bug bite with central punctum — bed bugs feed at night on exposed skin (face, neck, arms); reactions may be delayed days. Ask about travel/second-hand furniture.
dermnet_caption: Bed bug bite on the calf - note the central punctum
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Bed bug bite on the calf - note the central punctum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/bed-bugs

teaching_point: Bed bug bites in linear/clustered arrangement — eradication needs professional pest control (council or BPCA/NPTA member firm).
dermnet_caption: Bed bug bites on the calf
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Bed bug bites on the calf (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/bed-bugs

teaching_point: Fed adult bed bug (Cimex lectularius) — reddish-brown, apple-seed sized; hides in mattress seams, bed frames and furniture crevices (link to Week 3 Case 4).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Fed adult (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/bed-bugs

teaching_point: Bullous insect bite reaction — a more intense hypersensitivity; differential for blister beetle dermatitis (bite history, punctum, itch rather than burning).
